title: How many wickets did the bowler take in all?
description: A frequency table shows how many matches a bowler took 0, 1, 2 up to 7 wickets in. Reading the table, finding why adding 0 to 7 does not work, and adding a third column of wickets times matches gives the total number of wickets.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a frequency table, each row stands for many matches, so the total is found by multiplying the value by its frequency and adding. Watch for students who add only the first column.

video_script.why: The child reads a frequency table, sees why adding the values alone fails, and finds the total with a third column.
video_script.substitution: The table of wickets taken in matches is read and a third column of products is added.
video_script.anchor: a frequency table of the wickets a bowler took in the last thirty matches
video_script.payoff_line: The bowler took ninety wickets in the last thirty matches

final_answer.value: Title: wickets taken by a bowler in the last 30 matches; 3 matches; no, adding the wicket numbers ignores the matches; add a third column of products; total 90 wickets
final_answer.spoken: the bowler took ninety wickets in the last thirty matches

maths_rules: wickets and matches: 0 wickets in 2 matches, 1 in 4, 2 in 6, 3 in 8, 4 in 3, 5 in 5, 6 in 1, 7 in 1
adding 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 28 ignores the matches, so it is not the total
third column, wickets x matches: 0 x 2 = 0, 1 x 4 = 4, 2 x 6 = 12, 3 x 8 = 24, 4 x 3 = 12, 5 x 5 = 25, 6 x 1 = 6, 7 x 1 = 7
video_script.design: The frequency table is read first, then the wrong total is shown and its flaw named. A third column of products gives the right total, and the matches column is added to check it against thirty.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about cricket.
<bookmark mark='table'/>A child made a table of the wickets a bowler took in the last thirty matches.
<bookmark mark='ball'/>In some matches the bowler took no wickets, and in one match took seven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many wickets did the bowler take in all?

beats.on_screen: the table stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the table moves to the side; each row reads: a number of wickets and the number of matches in which it happened

marks.way: the table moves to the side
marks.row: one row is lit and read as wickets in some matches

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='row'/>We read each row of the table carefully. The matches column is called the frequency.

beats.on_screen: Given: wickets 0 to 7 in 2, 4, 6, 8, 3, 5, 1, 1 matches; 30 matches in all

marks.given: the table is written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the table of wickets and matches, for thirty matches in all.

beats.on_screen: To find: what the table says, the matches with 4 wickets, whether adding 0 to 7 works, and the total wickets
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to read the table, test a way of adding, and find the total wickets.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: read the table. Title: Wickets taken by a bowler in the last 30 matches. 4 wickets in 3 matches. 7 wickets in 1 match

marks.title: the title is written above the table
marks.four: the row of four wickets is lit and read as three matches
marks.seven: the row of seven wickets is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='title'/>Step one, read the table. A good title is, wickets taken by a bowler in the last thirty matches.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The row for four wickets shows three matches.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>One thing stands out. In one match, the bowler took seven wickets.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: test adding 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 28; but 3 wickets happened in 8 matches, so this misses the matches

marks.add: the numbers zero to seven are added to make twenty eight
marks.miss: an arrow shows that the row of three wickets stands for eight matches, not one
marks.no: the sum is crossed out in the warning colour

beats.removed: the sum of the first column is crossed out
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, test the idea of adding zero, one, two and so on up to seven. That makes twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='miss'/>But three wickets happened in eight matches, not in one.
<bookmark mark='no'/>Adding only the first column leaves out the matches. It cannot give the total.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: a third column, wickets x matches: 0, 4, 12, 24, 12, 25, 6, 7

marks.rule: a third column is added to the table
marks.first: the first four products are written
marks.rest: the last four products are written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, add a third column. Multiply the wickets by the matches in each row.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Zero times two is zero. One times four is four. Two times six is twelve, and three times eight is twenty four.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Four times three is twelve. Five times five is twenty five. Six times one is six, and seven times one is seven.

marks.add: the products are added one by one and each running total is written
marks.more: the later products are added the same way

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, add the third column. Zero and four make four, and twelve more make sixteen.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Twenty four more make forty, and twelve more make fifty two. Twenty five more make seventy seven.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Six more make eighty three, and seven more make ninety.

marks.add: the matches column is added, with running totals 6, 12, 20, 23, 28, 29, 30
marks.match: the total is joined to the thirty matches by a green line

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step five, check that the matches column adds up to thirty. Two, four, six and eight make twenty.
<bookmark mark='match'/>Three, five, one and one make ten more, so the total is thirty matches.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The bowler took ninety wickets in the last thirty matches

marks.ans: the total of the third column is boxed under the table

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The bowler took ninety wickets in the last thirty matches. We got it by adding the third column of wickets times matches.
